name: Germany

facts.religion: Catholic about 24%, Protestant about 22%, Muslim about 6%, no religion about 45%

snapshot: The far-right AfD won nearly 44 percent in Saxony-Anhalt in September 2026, three seats short of a majority, a heavy blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
culture: Germany's culture spans Goethe and Beethoven, the Bauhaus, Berlin's techno clubs and a beer and sausage tradition with regional variations. Football, especially the Bundesliga, is the top sport. Remembrance of the Holocaust is built into schooling and public life. Christmas markets and Oktoberfest are global exports.
society: Germany is Europe's largest economy, built on cars, machinery and chemicals, but it barely grew from 2023 to 2025 as cheap Russian gas vanished and Chinese competition rose. It took in more than a million refugees in 2015 to 2016 and again from Ukraine. The east, once communist, is poorer and older, and the AfD is strongest there.
situation: After 1945, West Germany built its politics around one rule above all: never again let extremists near power. Every mainstream party has kept a "firewall" against the far-right Alternative for Germany, which the domestic intelligence service has classified as extremist. In September 2026, in one eastern state, the voters came close to knocking that wall down.

On 6 September, the AfD won 43.8 percent in Saxony-Anhalt, nearly 23 points more than in 2021, taking 39 of 83 seats, just three short of a majority, after 24 years of CDU rule there (OSW). Its 35-year-old candidate Ulrich Siegmund, a TikTok natural, promised to bring back "our good, old, safe Germany" (Reuters via The Star). The result reflects the unhealed divide between east and west 36 years after reunification, and a rebuke of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose approval has sunk to record lows as his coalition struggles to revive Europe's largest economy, which barely grew for three years. Merz said the defeat shook his party "to its very foundations" but again ruled out working with the AfD; its co-leader Alice Weidel predicted he would be gone by Christmas (Ground News). Whether anyone can now form a government in Magdeburg without the AfD is uncertain; the small left-populist BSW has floated a non-partisan premier relying on shifting majorities. Trump posted the result on Truth Social without comment.
power: A federal parliamentary republic. The chancellor is elected by the Bundestag and leads the government; the Bundesrat represents the 16 states, which run schools, police and much else. The president is ceremonial.
holders: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU), leading a coalition with the SPD since May 2025.
